payload.purpose_context: An earlier decomposition of the runtime bridge left 36 thin forwarding functions behind so old test patches kept working. They serve no production caller, hide where logic really lives, and make tests silently patch the wrong place. This mission removes them, repoints every test and internal call at the owning seam, and keeps the two public entry points other parts of the CLI rely on.
payload.purpose_tldr: Delete the thin forwarding layer in the runtime bridge so every runtime seam owns its own symbols and tests patch the real owner.

options: Keep as public plain re-exports (same function objects)
payload.question: Do get_or_start_run and build_operational_context_for_claim stay on runtime_bridge, or are their CLI callers repointed at runtime_bridge_io?

payload.final_answer: Keep as public plain re-exports (same function objects). Operator brief: repointing callers outside src/runtime/next is out of scope; test_no_dead_symbols pins the facade names.

options: Run #2561 first; #2560 and #2562 follow as separate missions
payload.question: The tracker says #2561 is blockedBy #2560. Run #2561 first or wait?

payload.final_answer: Run #2561 first (operator orchestration ruling: mission 1 of 3). Editing the tracker blockedBy link is out of scope; the orchestrator reports it.

options: Module-qualified on the owning seam (one patch point = the owner)
payload.question: Inside src/runtime/next, how does code call a seam-owned name after its delegate is deleted?

payload.final_answer: Module-qualified on the owning seam (seam.name) everywhere inside src/runtime/next, including the bridge's own calls to get_or_start_run/build_operational_context_for_claim. The two bridge re-exports exist only for callers outside the package. Every test that patches the bridge re-export while driving a bridge-internal path is repointed (GROUNDING hazard 1).

options: No: per-site semantic refactor with call-path review
payload.question: Is this mission a bulk edit (change_mode: bulk_edit with an occurrence map)?

payload.final_answer: No. Each repoint needs call-path judgement (which binding the code under test looks up), adapters need behaviour preservation, and mechanism-only tests are deleted rather than renamed. A uniform string rename would be wrong at many sites; the acceptance gate test (static scan) is the guardrail instead of an occurrence map.

options: Static acceptance test per seam, strict-xfail until that seam is done, plus adapter characterisation tests
payload.question: How is red-first ATDD done for a deletion refactor?

payload.final_answer: A static acceptance test parametrized per seam (no delegate definitions in the bridge, no _rb back-edges to delegated names, re-export identity) lands first; seams not yet migrated are xfail(strict=True) and each seam WP removes its own xfail. Adapter characterisation tests land first and stay green throughout.
